dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: evam eva jagat sarvaṃ dagdhaṃ dhyātvā vikalpataḥ | ananyacetasaḥ puṃsaḥ pumbhāvaḥ paramo bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: In the same way, if one contemplates the whole world as burnt, with the mind on nothing else, the supreme state of being a person (pumbhāva) arises.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: in the previous dhāraṇā it was one's own body that was imagined burnt by Kālāgni; here it is the whole world. Śivopādhyāya glosses the 'highest state of man' as the nature of Bhairava, the unlimited subject. Wallis: 'imagining the whole world incinerated, a person of disciplined mind experiences the supreme state of the soul'.
dharana.technique_name: The Whole World Burnt by the Fire of Time
dharana.instruction: Observe only: read and understand this classical description. It is not practised in class. For practice, use Door 020.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 53 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The classical map is the whole world consumed, leaving only the unlimited knower. Drawn faint: studied, not drilled.
geometry.svg_hint: a faint circle of the world with a soft glow where it was; drawn faint to signal observe-only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Everything limited dissolves (described)
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the world of separate things pictured as falling away, leaving the knower. A picture to understand, not an exercise. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Study the verse; let the body simply rest while you do
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Understanding the image: all limited things dissolving, leaving the unlimited subject
attention.secondary: If sitting with anything, only the open space of Door 020

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: In the same way, if one contemplates the whole world as burnt, with the mind on nothing else, the supreme state of being a person (pumbhāva) arises.
adiyogi.method_summary: Classical method: following on from the previous verse, one contemplates the whole world as burnt by the same fire, with undivided mind, and the supreme state of the person arises. Observe-only in this school: read and understand it. For practice, use Door 020.

honesty.disclosure: Door 030 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 30 (verse 53) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 030 is dharana 30, verse 53. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

historical/observe_only: The classical method is a visualisation of the whole world being burnt. Imagery of the world's destruction can be distressing and is not used as a class drill. Taught as text to understand, not as a class drill.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Not led as a practice: imagery of the world's destruction can be distressing, especially in anxious or grieving times. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
safety.observe_only_note: Observe-only. Imagery of the whole world burning can be distressing; this school does not lead it. Read it as a description of everything limited dissolving. For practice, use Door 020 (space in every direction).

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 030: the whole world burnt by the fire of time. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 30, verse 53. This door is observe-only.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make, and no drill. Sit comfortably while we read. Its classical map is the whole world consumed, leaving the knower.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the body rest completely. Eyes open, reading or resting softly. Attention on understanding, not on doing.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath only. Nothing to practise with the breath here. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Hold the idea, not the image: everything limited can be seen as passing, while the one who knows remains.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: the limited passing, the knower remaining. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 53: describes contemplating the whole world as burnt, with undivided mind, and the supreme state of the person arising. Observe-only here. For practice, use Door 020.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Close the text. Take a normal breath. Look around the room and move on when ready.
